chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a believer who kills a believer intentionally: does he have repentance? So he said:

"If he killed him because of his faith, then there is no repentance for him. But if he killed him out of anger or because of some worldly matter, then his repentance is that retribution be taken from him. If it had not become known, he should go to the heirs of the slain and confess before them that he killed their companion. If they pardon him and do not kill him, he must give them the blood-money, free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and feed sixty needy persons, as repentance to Allah."

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: financial blood-money paid to the heirs
key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: repentance and return to Allah after sin
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: a needy person to be fed
key_terms.نَسَمَةً: a slave to be freed as expiation
key_terms.يُقَادَ مِنْهُ: legal retribution is carried out against him

ai.seo_question: What is the repentance for someone who intentionally kills a believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between killing a believer out of hostility to faith and killing out of anger or worldly motives. In the latter case, repentance requires submitting to legal accountability and, if pardoned, fulfilling financial and expiatory duties as repentance to Allah.
